title: Pronósticos en breve
text:
Prefacio


Este pequeño libro presenta algunas ideas del pronóstico de series temporales. También es una demostración práctica de quarto-i18n, una extensión de Quarto que mantiene las traducciones automáticas de un libro al día con su fuente en inglés.


El autor solo escribe los capítulos en inglés. Los demás idiomas los genera un traductor, los comprueba la herramienta y después los mejoran lectores que revisan párrafos y sugieren mejores redacciones.







TipPruébalo




Cambia a Français o Español en la barra lateral y elige Revisar esta página en el aviso de la parte superior de un capítulo. Cada párrafo muestra cuántas personas han revisado su traducción.




El material sigue el enfoque de Hyndman y Athanasopoulos (2021), disponible gratuitamente en línea.





Hyndman, Rob J., y George Athanasopoulos. 2021. Forecasting: Principles and Practice. 3rd ed. OTexts. https://otexts.com/fpp3/.

title: 1  Datos de series temporales
text: 1.1 Qué hace especial a una serie

title: 1  Datos de series temporales
text:
A diferencia de la mayoría de los conjuntos de datos, el orden de las observaciones importa. Cada valor está relacionado con los anteriores, y un pronóstico usa esa relación para decir algo sobre el futuro.


Hay tres características que aparecen una y otra vez:



Una tendencia es un aumento o una disminución a largo plazo de los datos.


La estacionalidad es un patrón que se repite con un periodo fijo, por ejemplo cada año o cada semana.


Un ciclo sube y baja sin un periodo fijo, a menudo a lo largo de varios años.

title: 1  Datos de series temporales
text:
1.2 Los datos de este libro

La mayoría de los ejemplos usan AirPassengers, un conjunto de datos clásico que viene con R. Registra el número de pasajeros aéreos internacionales de cada mes entre 1949 y 1960, en miles. La serie tiene {r} length(AirPassengers) observaciones.1







NotaFrecuencia




La frecuencia de una serie es el número de observaciones en un periodo estacional. Los datos mensuales tienen una frecuencia de 12.

title: 2  Visualizar una serie temporal
text:
2.1 Seasonal plots
# One line per year, coloured from earliest to latest
passengers$year <- format(passengers$month, "%Y")
passengers$month_of_year <- as.integer(format(passengers$month, "%m"))

ggplot(passengers, aes(x = month_of_year, y = count, group = year, colour = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Passengers (thousands)", colour = "Year")







Figura 2.2: Each year of the series drawn as its own line.

title: 2  Visualizar una serie temporal
text:
A seasonal plot draws each year as a separate line, so that the shape of the seasonal pattern is easier to compare from one year to the next.



July and August are the busiest months in every year of the data.

title: 3  Simple forecasting methods
text:
3.1 Naive and seasonal naive
h <- 24  # forecast horizon in months
last_year <- tail(as.numeric(AirPassengers), 12)

# Repeat the final year of data to cover the horizon
forecast_values <- rep(last_year, length.out = h)
future <- seq(as.Date("1961-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = h)

message(sprintf("Produced %d forecasts from %d observations", h, length(AirPassengers)))

Produced 24 forecasts from 144 observations

plot(future, forecast_values, type = "l",
     main = "Seasonal naive forecasts",
     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Passengers (thousands)")







Figura 3.1: Seasonal naive forecasts for the next two years.

title: 3  Simple forecasting methods
text:
The naive method uses the last observation as the forecast for every future period. The seasonal naive method instead uses the value from the same season of the last year, so a forecast for next July is this July’s value.



Because the series has a strong trend, the seasonal naive forecasts in Figura 3.1 are probably too low. A method that also models the trend would do better.

title: 3  Simple forecasting methods
text:
3.2 Measuring uncertainty

A single number hides how uncertain a forecast is. A prediction interval gives a range in which the future value is expected to lie with a stated probability, such as 80% or 95%. Intervals usually become wider as the forecast horizon increases, because uncertainty accumulates over time.

title: 4  How this book is translated
text: The author edits only the English .qmd files and _quarto.yml. Each translated language lives in a set of translation files under _i18n/, one file per chapter. Every paragraph, caption and code comment is a separate unit with its own source text, translation and list of reviewers.
crumbs: 4  How this book is translated

title: 4  How this book is translated
text:
4.2 Translating

Running i18n translate collects the units that are new or whose English text has changed. A translator fills them in, and the tool checks every result before it is accepted. Inline code, links, citations, cross-references and shortcodes must come back unchanged, and translated code must parse with R’s own parser.
crumbs: 4  How this book is translated

title: 4  How this book is translated
text:
4.3 Keeping translations honest

When a paragraph changes in English, its translation becomes stale. Readers then see the English paragraph, marked as such, until the unit is translated again. A translation is never silently wrong.


In code cells, only comments and display strings such as plot titles are translated. Variable names and data never change, so every language runs the same analysis. If a translated cell fails, the build uses the English cell.

title: 4  How this book is translated
text:
4.4 Reviewing

Choose Review this page in the notice to turn on reviewer mode. Each paragraph is marked by the number of people who have reviewed it. Select a paragraph to see the English source, then approve the translation or suggest a better one. Your changes are collected and submitted together as a pull request.







ImportantePull requests in this demo




This demo uses a local mock of the pull request service. It runs the same checks as the real service and saves each pull request on disk instead of opening it on GitHub.
